_doc: STAGING. The Nineteenth rebuilt vocabulary-first. This theme scored ZERO after the bench's other additions landed, and the diagnosis was theirs in general form: Juneteenth's identity IS proper nouns — Galveston, Granger, General Order No. 3, emancipation, jubilee, the parade — and every one dies to a 3-6 letter no-repeated-letter filter. The vocabulary was rebuilt from what survives: the food, the colour and the date. `red` sits in `named` because red food and drink is the day's recognised signifier, not background.

theme.name: The Nineteenth
theme.blurb: Two and a half years late to Galveston, and observed ever since in red — the drink, the cake, the whole table.

clues.stared: What the crowd does at the person holding the paper, every year, in silence
clues.read: Out loud, the same order, by whoever the elders have decided gets to
clues.date: The nineteenth, and the two and a half years it came late by
clues.red: The drink, the cake, the whole table, and the colour is the point
clues.star: On the flag, with the arc around it, and both mean something specific
clues.dares: What nobody does: talk through it, however long it runs

boards.scene: The park at ten in the morning

clues.hatred: Not the subject. The subject is what came after it, and who is still here
clues.date: Marked on a calendar in a kitchen, in pen, before it was a federal thing
clues.read: The proclamation, again, and the children are told to listen this time
clues.red: In the cooler, in the cake, on the shirts, and nobody had to be told
clues.heat: By ten it is already the main topic, and the tents went up at seven
clues.hat: Straw, wide, and lent to whoever forgot theirs within the first hour

boards.scene: The red drink, and what it used to be

clues.adores: What the whole table does to the one who brings it, without saying so
clues.soda: Big Red, strawberry, or whatever the store had, and the brand is not the point
clues.red: Hibiscus once, and the colour carried across an ocean before the flavour did
clues.read: The label, by a child, who is checking whether this is the real one
clues.does: What the grandmother insists the homemade one still has over the bottle
clues.roads: How far people drive for it, and the answer is further than it sounds

boards.scene: The cake, and who is allowed to cut it

clues.creamy: The icing, red, made from a recipe with no measurements written down
clues.cream: Red velvet, and the argument about cheese icing versus the older way
clues.year: Counted since 1865, out loud, by somebody doing the arithmetic wrong
clues.care: Taken over the first slice, which goes to the oldest person present
clues.acre: The park, and the corner of it this family has used since the sixties
clues.mace: In the spice tin, and it is in there for a reason nobody can explain

boards.scene: Getting there, and holding the spot

clues.packer: Whoever loaded the car, and they are not to be questioned about the order
clues.park: Claimed at seven with two tables and a cousin left behind to hold them
clues.cake: Travelled flat on the floor of the back seat, and it survived
clues.care: Taken with the cooler, which goes in last and comes out first
clues.rake: In the trunk, for the fire pit, from the uncle who plans for everything
clues.pace: Set by the drive, and everyone arrives already tired and already happy
